assignments.brief_reason: Removal justified by concern about kids reading cursing, not threats/toxicity or fairness standard across sides.
Describes a moderation approach that keeps opinions/attacks removed while expletives are reviewed rather than auto-removed, consistent with removing toxic/threatening content.
Accepts harsh language because there are no calls for violence/threats, aligning with violence/threat exceptions to free speech.
Explicitly aims to keep expression while removing hateful and violent language.
Uses a disinformation threshold while maintaining broad free speech; best fit is violence/threat exceptions, though the exception is misinformation-based.
Civility/offensiveness and name-calling drive removal, matching removal of excessively vulgar/toxic content.
Platform-withholding for being too extreme is not clearly about threats/violence/tosxicity or mirroring fairness.
Freedom of expression is conditioned on not harming others, aligning with allowing speech except harm/violence-related content.
Preference for discussion over provocation is not captured by the provided themes (threat/toxicity, violence exceptions, or cross-side fairness).
Personal attacks are disallowed while criticism is allowed, fitting removal of toxic/inflammatory content.
Combines fact-checking with a general rule about being 'downright mean' plus cuss words; 'mean'/'vulgarity' doesn’t map cleanly to the defined themes.
Evaluations depend on professionalism/fact-based writing rather than the threat/toxicity or violence-exception criteria.
Keeps constructive discussion and removes name-calling/purposefully inflammatory content, aligning with removing toxicity.
Focuses on calibrating intensity/out-of-proportion rather than specific threat/violence/toxicity categories.
Allows dialogue when tone isn’t too aggressive/vulgar and treats verbal attacks as improper, consistent with removing toxic/aggressive content.
Rejects both for sounding extremely extreme/too influential, which is not clearly threat/toxicity or violence/threat-based.
Removal decisions are driven by detecting offensive/incendiary language, fitting removal of toxic/inflammatory content.
Preference for facts over whining/crying is content quality-based and not explicitly tied to threats/violence/toxicity categories.
First Amendment framing and removal only tied to absence of harm fits the violence/threat-exception style allowance.
States profanity/bad language is the main influence, aligning with removal criteria related to vulgar/toxic language.
